This suggestion was originally advanced by John Lucas, who has had a substantial influence on Penrose. In this, as in several other areas, Lucas allowed his spirituality (he's a fairly devout Christian) to guide him to an improbable conclusion. My professional opinion (before I was an economist I trained as a philosopher, and indeed one of my research areas remains the philosophy of probability) is that Lucas'/Penrose's ideas in this area are based largely on a misconception of the modern formalist position.

Even if the brain used some as yet unknown branch of physics to achieve consciousness, it would still be a computer. It would just be a computer that used that branch of physics. If it were to turn out that some quantum property is required for consciousness, then we would build a quantum processor to create AI, which would inevitably turn against us and destroy us all.

Exactly. Unless the brain actually uses some supernatural process (not just currently unknown physics), it doesn't matter what crazy tricks it uses - those can be replicated by an artificial construct.

And if it can use supernatural processes then by definition we can't reason about them, since they don't follow an underlying set of rules. (If they did, then they wouldn't be supernatural.)

If you think your brain is more than a computer...

Then you've started from an unsupported basis, and you can continue to any subsequent position you like.

I work at a grocery store in 3 different departments, but primarily the bakery. I'm super bad at procrastinating and have been meaning to get this story up for ages but I'm probably finally getting around to it because someone died in the store today lol. Anyway.

One morning I was minding my own business doing my job when a horrifying grease golem of a man comes huffing up. Holy shit, this guy was seriously half grease. He had warts and zits all over his face, he was wearing an all grey outfit covered in grease stains, and his turkey neck was probably bigger than my head. So disgusting! He huffed and puffed his way up to our donut case and glanced around at it for a few seconds, before Siiiigggghiinnnnnggg super loudly. It was definitely one of those obvious 'I'm unhappy and I want your attention because of it' sighs.

So the coworker of mine who happened to be pulling all the donuts to the front of their trays at the time stands up and asks him the usual, hey how are you can I help you with something today? Right after she asks 'how are you' he interrupts her by loudly lamenting that he's super disappointed because we don't have plain cake donuts with maple glaze on them.

This thing, by the way, is super hard to understand. He's got so much fat pressing down on his throat that it makes him really hard to understand.

"Well sorry to hear that sir," replies my coworker, "but we only make them with sugar glaze and chocolate glaze. Maple glazed ones just do not sell so we don't make them."

The beast sighs loudly again, "Well they don't sell because you don't make them! You should make them, people would buy them and they wouldn't be disappointed."

No they wouldn't because we tried that before and, shocker, they didn't sell.

"I'm so disappointed you don't have them." he says with an air of finality. With the speed of a Man-of-War, he turns and slowly putters over to the deli and as with all unpleasant customers who leave our department, we stop thinking/caring about them. Not much later though we caught wind from our deli neighbors that he was being super picky about what chicken wings they grab for him (salt & vinegar flavor, of course).
He was just so disappointed, you guys!
